lore, by John Hobson Matthews, In the Preface of this
fascinating volume we read as follows:
“There are many good and popular English books on the
Mass. Some of them treat the subject after the manner of a
Rationale, explaining the significance of the prayers and
ceremonies of the eucharistic rites; others are historical and
antiquarian, and elucidate the origin and evolution of the
ceremonial—while of devotional works there is no end. It
appeared, however, that there was room for а short treatise
on the folklore and minor antiquities of the Mass; by which
аге meant the various aspects and the numerous details of
the Holy Sacrifice which have so impressed the minds of
Catholics in the past as to leave permanent traces in the
popular traditions and speech, The aim of this little book
is to stimulate love for the Mass by showing how it was
valued by our ancestors in the ages of faith, and what our
predecessors in the penal times willingly suffered for its sake.”
